did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 29 opens with the Philistines assembling at Aphek, while the army of Israel was camped at the spring near Jezreel. This describes the positions of the two armies as they prepared for battle.
Did you know? The Philistine commanders marched past their army in formations of hundreds and thousands, while David and his men followed behind with Achish, king of Gath.
Did you know? When the Philistine commanders noticed David, Achish reminded them that David had served him for a long time and that he had found no fault in him since the day he came to him.
Did you know? The Philistine commanders feared that David would become a “satan” to them in battle—that is, an obstacle or an enemy within—so they demanded that Achish send him back to his place.
Did you know? The Philistine commanders’ suspicion of David was reinforced by the famous song in Israel: “Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”

Did you know? Achish swore to David that he considered him an honest and good man, even comparing his loyalty to that of “an angel of God.” However, he was forced to yield to the position of the Philistine commanders.
Did you know? David protested to Achish, asking what he had done since coming to him, and even claiming that he should not be prevented from fighting the enemies of his lord the king.
Did you know? Achish ordered David and his men to rise early and leave at daylight, so that they would not join the Philistine army in battle.
Did you know? David and his men did rise early and return, while the Philistines continued on toward Jezreel. Thus David was prevented from taking part in the battle alongside the Philistines.
